items.title: If I can't get into the Thrawn Trilogy, should I stop trying with the post-ROTJ EU?
items.text:
If I can't get into the Thrawn Trilogy, should I stop trying with the post-ROTJ EU?
Hi guys! Long time lurker. I'm not a hardcore Star Wars guy, but I've seen some of TCW, and I used to looooove Ep 2 and 3 as a kid and I've seen those two a million times. I've tried exploring some of the EU/Canon stuff and I've liked some of the comics that I've read (but never obsessed.)

Of novels, I've read:

* Kenobi
* Heir to the Empire
* Before the Awakening
* Dark Forces - Soldier for the Empire
* Boba Fett #1: The Fight to Survive

I realize that the later 3 aren't really representative of most Star Wars books in quality, but I didn't like those three. I really **loved** Kenobi, and I *liked* Heir, but I never fell in love with it and it felt a little too long.

I've been trying and trying and trying to get through Dark Force Rising. I'm about 20% of the way through, and I just can't get farther. I don't even dislike the writing or the characters, but... I dunno! Something about it makes it hard for me to get through. I really want to check out some of the later post-ROTJ books (I love passing-the-torch sort of stories and I'm veeery excited to see a later generation of Jedi rise up and stuff), but I really have an issue getting into it.

I also reaaaally like the criminal underworld of Star Wars, so I wanna explore Coruscant Nights, Shadows of the Empire, the old school Han Solo books and stuff.

Most of my favorite novels are a bit lighter in tone or really experimental: (Redshirts, Agent to the Stars, Hitchhikers Guide to the Galaxy, etc.)

It's really early in the morning so I may have totally rambled: If I can't get through Dark Force Rising am I probably not going to really enjoy the rest post-ROTJ? 

(Additional question, what crime comics are there? I read the Blood Ties mini-series and I really liked it. I have an idea of what crime related novels to read, but I'm sure there's a toooon in the comics too. This can be EU and Canon, I don't care either way.)

Sorry for the ramble! Thanks!
Yeah, to be totally honest I’m cool with reading the [inferior] comic adaptation of the trilogy rather than skip it entirely. But do you think I’d enjoy the stuff after it?
Oh right, I’ve been meaning to try that! I liked Heir to be fair, but it never really captured me if that makes sense. I’ll check that out, thanks!

Yeah, that’s what I was wondering! I liked Heir enough (but I didn’t love it and it felt a bit too long), but I have just completely struggled with DFR.

I’ll try and push Dark Force Rising to see if I can start the ball rolling since I’m clearly not entirely adverse to the trilogy.

items.title: Updated Star Wars Comic Reading Order/Overlapping Guide?
items.text:
Updated Star Wars Comic Reading Order/Overlapping Guide?
Hey guys! Relatively new to the Star Wars canon here but I've read/seen some stuff. I'm looking to dive into the main comics, and I found this [handy reading guide.](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1nRUOniVBnA8h1e3u1X3w2lup7VM8RwpzrVVMFALfmEo/edit)

Thing is, it looks a little outdated. Would anyone be able to explain what other books overlap/intertwine after that so I don't end up confused and lost? I'm going to be reading in TPBs so Volume Names/Numbers are fine.

(Sidenote: I believe the only Star Wars Canon comics I've read were Shattered Empire and the Phasma mini, if that helps at all.)

I'm asking specifically for anything that might overlap like the Vader/Aphra/Star Wars books. It seems like anything else (like the Poe stuff and the Republic stuff) can be read in any order.
